      "author_utc": "2026-09-23T09:55:46Z",
      "body": "The third D-52 condition — every reader on one access point — was shown in\ne02c915. The export-identity gate and its four\n  tests are retired: there is no committed file left to compare.\n- The hosted CI hydrates the tracker, renders once and presets BEAD_RENDER;\n  every gate of the run reads that one render. Locally the access point\n  (scripts/bead_render.py) renders fresh through tools/bd, and without bd it\n  fails with both ways out — bootstrap or BEAD_RENDER — instead of reading a\n  stale copy.\n- The drift job hydrates too: plans-registry-strict reads the tracker, and\n  without the copy it would have crashed nightly. plans-registry and\n  plans-registry-strict declare needs_tracker; the schema now allows it in\n  both jobs.\n- The kit role geruest is dissolved: without the copy its remaining members\n  map to one export verdict, which the AK-6 test forbids. The stub files stay\n  with the export manifest. Two REIST_NICHT entries for tests that do not\n  travel were removed; the probe cap stays at 31.\n- verify_all.sh --ci measures the same gate set as the derived workflow\n  (finding 2 of the PR #32 review).\n- AGENTS.md house rules 2 and 4, README, plans/_README.md: the render is the\n  contract; a pull request body names every bead it opens, changes or closes\n  (maintainer, 2026-09-23, D-52 successor; the CI job summary follows as\n  bead coding-harness-1jg.4).\n- The empty gate-placement change package is archived (its bead 1jg.2 closed\n  with PR #32).\n\nStarted by a Cline session that stopped mid-way (uncommitted, last edit\n10:28); finished and corrected by Claude Code.\n\nVerified 2026-09-23: make verify VERIFY GREEN (325 passed, 15 skipped);\nverify_all.sh --job drift VERIFY GREEN, measuring the tracker locally.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "3e2a58ef23cdd4462882f640942e24a20d63618c": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-30T08:42:31Z",
      "body": "Mechanism A (rows L1-11, L3-1, L4-2, F6-1, F6-5): only the owner\nremoves the published holder record, and only while it still names the\nowner, so a cancelled waiter no longer deletes the active holder record;\nafter the protected command exits, a grandchild left in its process\ngroup is ended before the lock is released.\nMechanism B (rows L1-1, L1-12, F6-2): a nested marker is honoured only\nfor a related process: the holder is a live ancestor, or the process\nruns in the session the supervisor started for its child (now published\nwith the ownership), or it holds the inherited lock descriptor. An\nunrelated process naming the published pid takes ordinary admission.\nThe runner test that used a sibling holder now republishes the record\nnaming its own process.\nThree new tests were red before the fix and green after. The extra two\nhours were granted by the maintainer on 2026-10-30.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9E3xwLQJNC9qs5SWhu\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "3e2a58ef23cdd4462882f640942e24a20d63618c",
      "subject": "fix(verify-machine-lock): structural remedies for ownership lifetime and marker relation (bead coding-harness-p6mu)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/verify_lock.py",
        "tests/test_stage2.py",
        "tests/test_verify_lock.py"
      ]
    },

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",

      "touched_mapped_paths": [

        "decisions/gates.yaml",

        "scripts/ci_gates.py"

          "excerpt": "def _open_history() -> int:\n    \"\"\"A private regular history file for appending; an aliased or nonregular destination refuses.\n\n    The same shape as the admission's lock files: the no-follow open fails on\n    a symlink standing in the file's place, a FIFO cannot pass the regular\n    check, and nothing is ever written through a substituted destination.\n    \"\"\"\n    root = verify_lock.state_root()\n    try:\n        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the shared state directory {root} cannot be created ({error.strerror or error})\"\n        ) from error\n    if root.is_symlink() or not root.is_dir():\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the shared state directory {root} is not a usable directory\")\n    path = history_path()\n    try:\n        return os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)\n    except FileExistsError:\n        pass\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the history file {path} cannot be created no-follow ({error.strerror or error}) — \"\n            \"a substituted destination is refused, never written through\"\n        ) from error\n    # O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO standing in the file's place is refused below, never waited on.\n    try:\n        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the history file {path} is not a private regular file; refusing substituted history\"\n        ) from error\n    info = os.fstat(fd)\n    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_nlink != 1:\n        os.close(fd)\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the history file {path} is not an unaliased regular file; refusing substituted history\")\n    return fd\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::plan_reuse",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_reuse_requires_the_exact_binding_seat_model_and_prompt(store, repo):\n    k = key(\"s1\")\n    make_source(store, repo, results=[(k, terminal(k))])\n    source, plan = resume(store, repo, [k])\n    assert source.usable and set(plan.reused) == {\"s1\"} and plan.not_reused == []\n    assert plan.reused[\"s1\"][\"report\"] == \"REPORT\"\n    for field, other in [\n        (\"stage\", \"map\"),\n        (\"topic\", 2),\n        (\"seat\", 1),\n        (\"endpoint\", \"claude\"),\n        (\"model\", \"m-2\"),\n        (\"prompt_sha256\", hashlib.sha256(b\"other\").hexdigest()),\n    ]:\n        planned = {**k, field: other}\n        _, plan = resume(store, repo, [planned])\n        assert plan.reused == {}, field\n        assert [reason for _, reason in plan.not_reused] == [field.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")], field\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

Linked tests are the test files the\n    touch map links to a touched path, in the working tree and, for a path the repair removed, at the\n    baseline; every surviving touched or linked test file runs whole. A prompt, shared test or\n    execution configuration, an input kind outside Python and the documents, production code with no\n    linked test, an aliased file or an unreadable inventory makes the check full instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def full(reason: str) -> Targeted:\n        return Targeted([], [], [], reason)\n\n    try:\n        touched = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env, against=against))\n        if any(0xDC80 <= ord(char) <= 0xDCFF for path in touched for char in path):\n            return full(\"a changed Git path cannot be decoded safely\")\n        before = _baseline_inventory(root, env, against)\n    except (Refused, OSError, touch_map.CannotMeasure) as error:\n        return full(f\"the touched paths could not be listed ({error})\")\n    resolved = root.resolve()\n    present: dict[str, bool] = {}\n    touched_tests: list[str] = []\n    code: list[str] = []\n    python: list[str] = []\n    for posix in touched:\n        name = posix.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[-1]\n        if posix.startswith(\"prompts/\"):\n            return full(\"a prompt changed\")\n        if posix in SHARED_INFRASTRUCTURE:\n            return full(f\"`{posix}` is shared execution infrastructure\")\n        if name == \"conftest.py\":\n            return full(f\"`{posix}` is shared test configuration\")\n        path = root / posix\n        try:\n            if path.is_symlink():\n                return full(f\"`{posix}` is a link\")\n            present[posix] = path.exists()\n            if present[posix] and (\n                not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_nlink != 1 or path.resolve() != resolved / posix\n            ):\n                return full(f\"`{posix}` is not an ordinary single-linked file\")\n        except touch_map.links(touch_map.WorktreeSnapshot(str(root), env=env, timeout=GIT_SECONDS)) | touch_map.links(\n            touch_map.Snapshot(str(root), against, env=env, timeout=GIT_SECONDS)\n        )\n    except (touch_map.CannotMeasure, OSError, ValueError, RecursionError) as error:\n        return full(f\"the link inventory could not be read ({error})\")\n    touched_set = set(touched)\n    linked: dict[str, set[str]] = {}\n    for source, target, _kind in edges:\n        if target in touched_set and _is_test_module(source) and (root / source).is_file():\n            linked.setdefault(target, set()).add(source)\n    for posix in code:\n        if not linked.get(posix):\n            return full(f\"`{posix}` has no linked test\")\n    tests = needs the admitted full check's budget.           "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing};           "excerpt": "def verify_evidence(done: subprocess.CompletedProcess, key: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The bounded evidence of a red post-run check (`make verify`, or the draft's document check).\n\n    It renders the framed gates that blocked, else the run's tail.\n\n    Read the active denylist at diagnostic emission time and raise Refused fail-closed if\n    protection refuses, on every route including keyless routes (key=None). The complete\n    concatenated streams are checked before reduction; their mapped boundary retains framing.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Protected whole, before any reduction: a cut must not split a multiline match and leave a part of it.\n    raw_stdout = done.stdout or \"\"\n    output, boundary = _protect_diagnostics(raw_stdout + (done.stderr or \"\"), key, len(raw_stdout))\n    stdout, stderr = output[:boundary], output[boundary:]\n    # verify_all.sh frames gates on standard output; a gate's standard error arrives unframed after them.\n    red = red_sections(stdout)\n    if red is None:\n        return scrub(\"\\n\".join(output.splitlines()[-TAIL_LINES:]), key)\n    evidence = \"The gates that blocked, each with its last lines:\\n\" + red\n    errors = stderr.splitlines()\n    if errors:\n        # Unframed: the last lines of the whole run's standard error, not of the blocking gate alone.\n        cut = len(errors) - STDERR_LINES\n        kept = ([f\"[… {cut} earlier lines left out …]\"] if cut > 0 else []) + errors[-STDERR_LINES:]\n        evidence += \"\\n\\nStandard error of the whole run, last lines:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(kept)\n    return scrub(evidence, key)\n",

a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing};           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Verification runs through git and CI, not through the harness",
          "end_line": 605,
          "excerpt": "### Verification runs through git and CI, not through the harness\n\n```bash\nmake verify     # local gates, cheap first; stop at the first blocking failure\nmake gates      # what the CI runs, read from decisions/gates.yaml; a `writer` gate is marked\nmake staleness  # hygiene of the plans/ artefacts\nmake index      # regenerate plans/INDEX.md\n```\n\n`make` holds **no list of its own**. It calls `scripts/verify_all.sh`, which asks\n`scripts/ci_gates.py`, which reads `decisions/gates.yaml` — the same file\n`ci.yml` is generated from, and a hand edit of `ci.yml` fails the `ci-drift`\ngate. A second list is the reason local runs and CI drift apart — not its\nsymptom.\n\nLocal verification orders selected gates by declared cost (`seconds` before\n`minutes`) and stops at the first blocking failure. It names every remaining\nselected gate as not run because of that failure; a red run is therefore not\na complete check. Hosted CI and `--ci` continue through all selected gates.\nSee the [gate catalog](governance/gate-catalog.md) for costs and enforcement.\n\nCI runs on pull requests (a superseded run is cancelled) and on pushes to\n`main`, under Python 3.12; a branch without a pull request gets no hosted run,\nand the schedule runs only the drift gates.\n\n**One admission per user and machine** (bead coding-harness-p6mu). Before its\ngates, `verify_all.sh` hands the run to `scripts.verify_lock`: protected work\nof one user on one machine queues in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/`\n— shared across repositories and worktrees, so the three-lane trial's\nconcurrent full checks cannot happen again. Waiters are admitted in\nregistration order; while waiting, an entry logs its wait immediately and\nevery five minutes, naming the holder's process id, command and start time.\nA nested protected entry — a check descended from a live admission — carries\n`HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD=<holder-pid>` and reuses its ancestor's admission\ninstead of deadlocking on it; a stale or unrelated marker uses ordinary\nadmission. After the lock, admission reads the system's free memory (macOS\n`memory_pressure`'s system-wide free percentage, Linux `MemAvailable` over\n`MemTotal`) and waits, rechecking every 30 seconds, while readings sit below\nthe floor — 25 percent by default, or `HARNESS_VERIFY_MEMORY_FLOOR` as a\nfinite percentage in `[0, 100]`, equality admitting. Readings below the floor\nfor 60 minutes from the first low one refuse the entry, naming the floor and\nthe last reading; a reading that cannot be taken is logged and the entry\nproceeds. Unusable state — a substituted or unwritable lock, holder or queue\nfile — refuses the entry before any protected work instead of running\nunlocked. Ownership ends only when the protected work and its children stop,\nincluding on failure, cancellation and signals, so a dead entry never blocks\nthe next one. The queue and memory waits consume no runner step limit and no\npytest proof's execution timeout; the configured limits still bind the\nexecuting check. Hosted CI is untouched: its gate steps never enter the\nrunner's shell path, and nothing disables admission because CI is set.\n\nVerification durations are appended locally to `verify-duration.jsonl` in\nthat shared state directory. Each run records gate and execution durations,\noutcomes, revision, configuration and machine context; admission wait is\nreported separately, with inherited waits marked as reused. Read summaries\nwith `python3 -m scripts.verify_duration report`, or inspect one run with\n`python3 -m scripts.verify_duration report --run <run-id>`. Interrupted runs\nremain incomplete, and malformed rows are diagnosed. Unusable measurement\nstorage warns without changing gate execution or verdicts; raw history stays\noutside Git.\n\nThe stop hook is the comfort layer, not the enforcement. It runs only when\nPython was touched since `HEAD`: a hook that costs a minute when nothing has\nhappened is switched off within a week — and a switched-off hook is worse than\nnone, because the registry ke",

A failed gate keeps its raw exit status — an advisory failure is not a pass.\n    code, _, _ = _run(\n        capsys,\n        \"gate\",\n        \"--run\",\n        first.strip(),\n        \"--gate\",\n        \"probe\",\n        \"--start\",\n        \"0.0\",\n        \"--end\",\n        \"2.0\",\n        \"--status\",\n        \"3\",\n        \"--enforcement\",\n        \"advisory\",\n    )\n    assert code == 0\n    gates = [event for event in _history(state) if event[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert len(gates) == 1\n    assert gates[0][\"exit\"] == 3 and gates[0][\"enforcement\"] == \"advisory\" and gates[0][\"seconds\"] == 2.0\n\n    #           "excerpt": "### Verification runs through git and CI, not through the harness\n\n```bash\nmake verify     # local gates, cheap first; stop at the first blocking failure\nmake gates      # what the CI runs, read from decisions/gates.yaml; a `writer` gate is marked\nmake staleness  # hygiene of the plans/ artefacts\nmake index      # regenerate plans/INDEX.md\n```\n\n`make` holds **no list of its own**. It calls `scripts/verify_all.sh`, which asks\n`scripts/ci_gates.py`, which reads `decisions/gates.yaml` — the same file\n`ci.yml` is generated from, and a hand edit of `ci.yml` fails the `ci-drift`\ngate. A second list is the reason local runs and CI drift apart — not its\nsymptom.\n\nLocal verification orders selected gates by declared cost (`seconds` before\n`minutes`) and stops at the first blocking failure. It names every remaining\nselected gate as not run because of that failure; a red run is therefore not\na complete check. Hosted CI and `--ci` continue through all selected gates.\nSee the [gate catalog](governance/gate-catalog.md) for costs and enforcement.\n\nCI runs on pull requests (a superseded run is cancelled) and on pushes to\n`main`, under Python 3.12; a branch without a pull request gets no hosted run,\nand the schedule runs only the drift gates.\n\n**One admission per user and machine** (bead coding-harness-p6mu). Before its\ngates, `verify_all.sh` hands the run to `scripts.verify_lock`: protected work\nof one user on one machine queues in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/`\n— shared across repositories and worktrees, so the three-lane trial's\nconcurrent full checks cannot happen again. Waiters are admitted in\nregistration order; while waiting, an entry logs its wait immediately and\nevery five minutes, naming the holder's process id, command and start time.\nA nested protected entry — a check descended from a live admission — carries\n`HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD=<holder-pid>` and reuses its ancestor's admission\ninstead of deadlocking on it; a stale or unrelated marker uses ordinary\nadmission. After the lock, admission reads the system's free memory (macOS\n`memory_pressure`'s system-wide free percentage, Linux `MemAvailable` over\n`MemTotal`) and waits, rechecking every 30 seconds, while readings sit below\nthe floor — 25 percent by default, or `HARNESS_VERIFY_MEMORY_FLOOR` as a\nfinite percentage in `[0, 100]`, equality admitting. Readings below the floor\nfor 60 minutes from the first low one refuse the entry, naming the floor and\nthe last reading; a reading that cannot be taken is logged and the entry\nproceeds. Unusable state — a substituted or unwritable lock, holder or queue\nfile — refuses the entry before any protected work instead of running\nunlocked. Ownership ends only when the protected work and its children stop,\nincluding on failure, cancellation and signals, so a dead entry never blocks\nthe next one.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided.           "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again.           "excerpt": "def gates() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Alle Gates der einen Liste, in ihrer Reihenfolge.\"\"\"\n    fehler = validate_schema()\n    if fehler:\n        raise ValueError(\"Gate-Datei verletzt das Schema: \" + \"; \".join(fehler))\n    doc = yaml.safe_load(GATE_FILE.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for g in doc[\"gates\"]:\n        aktion = g.get(\"action\")\n        kommando = g.get(\"command\")\n        ersatz = _lokales_kommando(aktion, g.get(\"with\")) if aktion else None\n        out.append(\n            {\n                \"id\": g[\"id\"],\n                \"name\": g[\"title\"],\n                \"job\": g[\"job\"],\n                \"command\": kommando if kommando else ersatz,\n                \"action\": aktion,\n                \"with\": g.get(\"with\") or {},\n                \"enforcement\": g[\"enforcement\"],\n                \"floor\": g[\"floor\"],\n                \"placement\": g[\"placement\"],\n                \"cost\": g[\"cost\"],\n                \"needs_tracker\": bool(g.get(\"needs_tracker\")),\n                \"needs_history\": bool(g.get(\"needs_history\")),\n                \"subsets\": list(g.get(\"subsets\") or []),\n                \"reason\": g.get(\"reason\", \"\"),\n                \"local_runnable\": kommando is not None or ersatz is not None,\n                \"via_local_equivalent\": ersatz is not None,\n            }\n        )\n    return out\n",

          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md",
          "reference": "The target picture",
          "start_line": 149,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],

          "excerpt": "def test_early_stop_history_records_only_executed_gates(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 9: the history of an early-stopped run measures only executed gates and ends red.\n\n    The skipped minutes gates produce no duration events, the one executed\n    seconds gate does, and the run-end record exists with the red verdict —\n    the stop is never mistaken for a finished green run.\n    \"\"\"\n    base = tmp_path / \"history\"\n    gates = [\n        _gate(base, \"suite-minutes\", \"minutes\"),\n        _gate(base, \"quick-red\", \"seconds\", ending=\"exit 1\"),\n        _gate(base, \"after-minutes\", \"minutes\"),\n    ]\n    tree = _tree_files(base / \"tree\")\n    _write_gate_file(tree, gates)\n    done = _run_runner(tree)\n    assert done.returncode == 1, f\"exit {done.returncode}\\n{done.stdout}\\n{done.stderr}\"\n    events = _tree_history(tree)\n    starts = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"run_start\"]\n    assert len(starts) == 1 and starts[0][\"job\"] == \"verify\" and starts[0][\"placement\"] == \"local\"\n    run_id = starts[0][\"run_id\"]\n    gate_rows = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert [e[\"gate\"] for e in gate_rows] == [\"quick-red\"], \"the history fabricated an event for a skipped gate\"\n    assert all(row[\"run_id\"] == run_id for row in gate_rows)\n    assert gate_rows[0][\"exit\"] == 1 and isinstance(gate_rows[0][\"seconds\"], int | float)\n    ends = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"run_end\"]\n    assert len(ends) == 1 and ends[0][\"run_id\"] == run_id and ends[0][\"verdict\"] == \"red\"\n",

The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. New\n    files are added intent-to-add for the gates and dropped afterwards; a refusal of the admission,\n    a timeout and a red exit are problems; a `make` that cannot be started raises `CallFailed`.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission([\"make\", \"verify\"]) as owned:\n            try:\n                intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n            except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n                return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n            done = launch(\n                [\"make\", \"verify\"],\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` was not started: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    else:\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

Readings below the floor\nfor 60 minutes from the first low one refuse the entry, naming the floor and\nthe last reading; a reading that cannot be taken is logged and the entry\nproceeds. Unusable state — a substituted or unwritable lock, holder or queue\nfile — refuses the entry before any protected work instead of running\nunlocked.           "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

A second list is the reason local runs and CI drift apart — not its\nsymptom.\n\nLocal verification orders selected gates by declared cost (`seconds` before\n`minutes`) and stops at the first blocking failure. It names every remaining\nselected gate as not run because of that failure; a red run is therefore not\na complete check. Hosted CI and `--ci` continue through all selected gates.\nSee the [gate catalog](governance/gate-catalog.md) for costs and enforcement.\n\nCI runs on pull requests (a superseded run is cancelled) and on pushes to\n`main`, under Python 3.12; a branch without a pull request gets no hosted run,\nand the schedule runs only the drift gates.\n\n**One admission per user and machine** (bead coding-harness-p6mu). Before its\ngates, `verify_all.sh` hands the run to `scripts.verify_lock`: protected work\nof one user on one machine queues in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/`\n— shared across repositories and worktrees, so the three-lane trial's\nconcurrent full checks cannot happen again. Waiters are admitted in\nregistration order; while waiting, an entry logs its wait immediately and\nevery five minutes, naming the holder's process id, command and start time.\nA nested protected entry — a check descended from a live admission — carries\n`HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD=<holder-pid>` and reuses its ancestor's admission\ninstead of deadlocking on it; a stale or unrelated marker uses ordinary\nadmission. After the lock, admission reads the system's free memory (macOS\n`memory_pressure`'s system-wide free percentage, Linux `MemAvailable` over\n`MemTotal`) and waits, rechecking every 30 seconds, while readings sit below\nthe floor — 25 percent by default, or `HARNESS_VERIFY_MEMORY_FLOOR` as a\nfinite percentage in `[0, 100]`, equality admitting. Readings below the floor\nfor 60 minutes from the first low one refuse the entry, naming the floor and\nthe last reading; a reading that cannot be taken is logged and the entry\nproceeds. Unusable state — a substituted or unwritable lock, holder or queue\nfile — refuses the entry before any protected work instead of running\nunlocked. Ownership ends only when the protected work and its children stop,\nincluding on failure, cancellation and signals, so a dead entry never blocks\nthe next one. The queue and memory waits consume no runner step limit and no\npytest proof's execution timeout; the configured limits still bind the\nexecuting check. Hosted CI is untouched: its gate steps never enter the\nrunner's shell path, and nothing disables admission because CI is set.\n\nVerification durations are appended locally to `verify-duration.jsonl` in\nthat shared state directory. Each run records gate and execution durations,\noutcomes, revision, configuration and machine context; admission wait is\nreported separately, with inherited waits marked as reused. Read summaries\nwith `python3 -m scripts.verify_duration report`, or inspect one run with\n`python3 -m scripts.verify_duration report --run <run-id>`. Interrupted runs\nremain incomplete, and malformed rows are diagnosed. Unusable measurement\nstorage warns without changing gate execution or verdicts; raw history stays\noutside Git.\n\nThe stop hook is the comfort layer, not the enforcement.           "end_line": 158,
          "excerpt": "## Boundary\n\nDecided by the maintainer on 2026-10-30 after repeated phase-6 rows on one\nmechanism (protected descendants outliving the admission). The admission\nprotects the machine's load, not data: an overlap of two checks costs time,\nnever correctness.\n\n- Covered: normal exit, failure, cancellation and trapped signals (SIGINT,\n  SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT) end the protected command's process group before\n  release; a grandchild left in that group after the command exits is ended\n  before release, by the supervisor and by the runner's timed launches. A trapped\n  signal that arrives while the protected command is being started is held back\n  until the command is registered for cleanup, in the supervisor as in the runner\n  (phase-6 row F6-9).\n- Accepted limit, signal timing (maintainer, 2026-10-30): after that deferral, a\n  further finding about the moment a signal arrives is an accepted limit, not a\n  finding: the lock protects the machine's load, never data.\n- Accepted limit: when an intermediate process is killed hard (SIGKILL) while\n  its own descendants run in another process group or session, those\n  descendants can outlive the admission and briefly overlap a successor. Their\n  time is bounded by the runner's step limits. A review row that describes\n  only this case is an accepted limit, not a finding.\n- A process container that would close the limit (cgroups, job objects) is out\n  of scope until the run report measures such overlaps in practice.\n\n",

        }

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When a selected gate command finishes, the console identifies that gate's measured seconds and raw pass/fail result.\n   *Refuted by:* a failed advisory gate has no duration, is labelled passed, or an unexecuted gate is presented as measured.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-1.\n\n2. When an admitted run reaches its final verdict, the console reports execution seconds separately from admission wait.\n   *Refuted by:* an injected admission delay increases reported execution seconds, or clock adjustments produce negative gate seconds.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-1; decisions.md#Q-2.\n\n3. When measurement storage is usable, each run appends identifiable gate measurements and its completion outcome to local history outside the repository in the verification admission's state directory.\n   *Refuted by:* a second run replaces the first, concurrent or nested runs mix identities, a listing-only invocation adds a run, or an interrupted run is represented as complete.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2.\n\n4. When a measurement is recorded, it is attributable to its UTC date, commit, dirty state, gate configuration, job, placement, gate or run identity, seconds and result.\n   *Refuted by:* runs of different jobs or dirty trees cannot be distinguished, or a failed command loses its exit status in history.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2; decisions.md#Q-3.\n\n5. When an admitted run starts measuring, its records carry free-memory percentage at execution start, the effective worker setting and admission wait with its admission identity and reuse status, using explicit unknown values for unavailable readings.\n   *Refuted by:* unavailable memory becomes zero, a worker override is replaced by a guessed count, or a nested run's inherited wait is attributed to gate execution.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2.\n\n6. When the local history reader selects a run, it shows its per-gate and execution durations, outcomes and machine context without treating missing completion or malformed history as a successful complete run.\n   *Refuted by:* a truncated final row crashes the reader or makes an unfinished run eligible as baseline evidence.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2; decisions.md#Q-3.\n\n7. If measurement storage cannot be used, the runner visibly reports the missing history while retaining the gate commands' existing execution and verdict behavior.\n   *Refuted by:* an append failure suppresses a gate, changes its enforcement, hides missing history, or writes through a substituted history-file symlink.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-1; decisions.md#Q-2.\n\n8. When timing is enabled for verify, docs or drift, the runner retains gate selection, order, blocking versus advisory enforcement, worker overrides and the existing shared admission behavior.\n   *Refuted by:* a failed blocking gate becomes green, later gates stop running after an advisory failure, or inherited admission queues behind itself.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-1; decisions.md#Q-2.\n\n9.           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When independent protected entries use the same shared state, at most one\n   admission's protected work executes at a time across repositories and worktrees.\n   *Refuted by:* overlapping gate/pytest intervals from independent admissions.\n\n2. When several live entries wait, they are admitted in registration order\n   without runner priority.\n   *Refuted by:* a later registered waiter overtaking an earlier live waiter.\n\n3. While an entry waits for another holder, it logs the wait immediately and\n   at least every five minutes, identifying the holder's process id, command\n   and start time whenever a holder exists.\n   *Refuted by:* a silent wait, a missing five-minute update, or missing holder\n   identity despite an active holder with published metadata.\n\n4. When a runner check finally starts, its configured execution time limit\n   is available in full regardless of time spent in admission.\n   *Refuted by:* queue or memory waiting causing a short passing check to time\n   out, or removal of the existing limit on a hung executing check.\n\n5. When nested work inherits a valid held marker, it uses its ancestor's\n   admission without another queue or memory wait.\n   *Refuted by:* a nested copied runner deadlocking or rechecking memory; an\n   absent, malformed, stale or unrelated marker bypassing admission.\n\n6. When a protected invocation finishes, fails or is interrupted, remaining\n   live waiters can proceed without manual stale-lock or dead-waiter cleanup.\n   *Refuted by:* a dead holder/waiter blocking progress, or releasing ownership\n   while its protected child workload still runs.\n\n7. When a memory reading is available, admission uses macOS\n   `memory_pressure`'s system-wide free percentage or Linux\n   `MemAvailable / MemTotal * 100`, according to the host platform.\n   *Refuted by:* substituting another macOS percentage, Linux `MemFree`, or\n   accepting malformed/non-finite values as a usable reading.\n\n8. While usable available-memory readings are below the configured floor,\n   admission retains the lock and waits, logging and rechecking every 30 seconds.\n   *Refuted by:* protected work starting on a below-floor reading or another\n   admission entering while the first waits for memory.\n\n9. If usable memory readings remain below the floor for 60 minutes from the\n   first low reading, admission refuses without starting protected work and\n   names the floor and last reading.\n   *Refuted by:* a workload starting, an unbounded low-memory wait, or refusal\n   without the two percentages; a qualifying reading before the deadline must\n   instead allow work to start.\n\n10. If memory cannot be measured, admission logs that fact and proceeds.\n    *Refuted by:* an unavailable, failed, hung, unsupported or malformed probe\n    hanging/refusing the run or being silently treated as a valid percentage.\n\n11. When no override is provided, the floor is 25 percent, with equality\n    sufficient for admission.\n    *Refuted by:* a usable reading below 25 starting work, or exactly 25 waiting.\n\n12. When `HARNESS_VERIFY_MEMORY_FLOOR` supplies a finite percentage in\n    `[0, 100]`, admission uses that value; an invalid override refuses explicitly.\n    *Refuted by:* ignoring a valid override or silently accepting an invalid one.\n\n13. When protected work completes, the wrapper preserves its existing success\n    or failure verdict and gate selection, including hosted CI.\n    *Refuted by:* turning a failed check green, changing placement/enforcement,\n    adding a second command list, or disabling admission merely because CI is set.\n\n14. If shared locking or queue state cannot be used safely, the entry refuses\n    with a diagnostic before protected work starts.\n    *Refuted by:* falling through unlocked after a state-directory, lock or\n    queue error, or following a substituted state file to overwrite another file.\n\n",

          "end_line": 158,
          "excerpt": "## Boundary\n\nDecided by the maintainer on 2026-10-30 after repeated phase-6 rows on one\nmechanism (protected descendants outliving the admission). The admission\nprotects the machine's load, not data: an overlap of two checks costs time,\nnever correctness.\n\n- Covered: normal exit, failure, cancellation and trapped signals (SIGINT,\n  SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT) end the protected command's process group before\n  release; a grandchild left in that group after the command exits is ended\n  before release, by the supervisor and by the runner's timed launches. A trapped\n  signal that arrives while the protected command is being started is held back\n  until the command is registered for cleanup, in the supervisor as in the runner\n  (phase-6 row F6-9).\n- Accepted limit, signal timing (maintainer, 2026-10-30): after that deferral, a\n  further finding about the moment a signal arrives is an accepted limit, not a\n  finding: the lock protects the machine's load, never data.\n- Accepted limit: when an intermediate process is killed hard (SIGKILL) while\n  its own descendants run in another process group or session, those\n  descendants can outlive the admission and briefly overlap a successor. Their\n  time is bounded by the runner's step limits. A review row that describes\n  only this case is an accepted limit, not a finding.\n- A process container that would close the limit (cgroups, job objects) is out\n  of scope until the run report measures such overlaps in practice.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-verify-machine-lock/spec.md",
          "reference": "Boundary",
          "start_line": 134,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing};           "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- Speeding up successful gates, reducing test coverage, selecting gates\n  from changed files, caching results or promising a total runtime target.\n- Changing admission locks, worker sizing, duration storage schema,\n  targeted repair scheduling, hosted CI coverage or enforcement levels.\n- Automatic cost estimation, additional cost classes or sorting by live\n  timings. Future reclassification remains an explicit gate-list edit.\n- Migrating sibling repositories or reading or modifying a user-level stop\n  hook.           "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Proposed order of work\n\nOrdered by effect per effort, from the figures above. Each step names the\nbead that already holds it.\n\n1. **Now, small and independent of the strategy research.**\n   - Cheap gates before the test gate inside `make verify`, and stop at the\n     first red blocking gate. No bead yet. Saves the 3.3 hours seen above and\n     shortens every red run.\n   - Clean up after a run: remove the run's own temporary folders; refuse\n     admission under a free-disk bound (bead coding-harness-87b0, open).\n   - Remove merged worktrees (the rule exists in `AGENTS.md`; 91 stand).\n   - Two slots (bead coding-harness-u1ha) as decided — a stopgap, measured\n     as its decisions record demands.\n2. **Fewer full runs (the largest lever).**\n   - Targeted check after implement and draft (bead coding-harness-0swp,\n     P1). With the median of seven runs per change, moving the attempts to\n     layer 2 removes most of the demand.\n   - Reuse of a green full result by content key (extends bead\n     coding-harness-43iz from \"non-test gates per commit\" to \"the whole\n     verdict per tree content\").\n   - Formalities fixed and checked before anything else (bead\n     coding-harness-7ftj).\n3. **A shorter full run.**\n   - Shared fixture for the research-swarm tests (bead coding-harness-wnka):\n     eleven of the twelve slowest tests are in that one file (baseline note).\n   - Kit probe only when kit files changed, hosted CI keeps it always (bead\n     coding-harness-w2ay): 200 s per run.\n   - Worker memory measured, so the cap of four may rise (bead\n     coding-harness-351h).\n4. **Capacity outside the machine.**\n   - Full check in hosted CI as the evidence for phase 6 (bead\n     coding-harness-u3qg; its blocker, coding-harness-wkxm, is closed). It\n     needs a workflow change, which is the maintainer's file.\n5. **Hold the gain.**\n   - Budget and test layers as a decision (the ADR proposal of bead\n     coding-harness-1ga5), with a gate that fails when the budget is broken.\n   - A weekly reading of the run log — runs per day, runs per change, wait,\n     duration — in the handover (bead coding-harness-zaqf).\n   - Coverage-based selection (bead coding-harness-s3kf) only if layer 2\n     still misses tests after step 2.\n\nAdmission order and the wait alarm (bead coding-harness-ofmz) and a general\njob admission (bead coding-harness-wpb0) stay useful for machine load, but\nthey lose urgency for the full check once steps 1 and 2 hold.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_repository_gate_schema_is_v3() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Final activation test of verify-cheap-first (criteria 1 and 10 of its spec).\n\n    The real gate list declares schema 3 with a cost on every gate: pytest and\n    the kit probe are the minutes class, every other current gate seconds. And once schema 3 is active, a version-2 list is\n    rejected, not accepted.\n    \"\"\"\n    doc = yaml.safe_load(ci_gates.GATE_FILE.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    assert doc[\"schema_version\"] == 3, doc.get(\"schema_version\")\n    kosten = {g[\"id\"]: g.get(\"cost\") for g in doc[\"gates\"]}\n    assert set(kosten.values()) == {\"seconds\", \"minutes\"}, kosten\n    assert kosten[\"pytest\"] == \"minutes\", \"pytest is the minutes class of the duration baseline (2026-11-05)\"\n    assert kosten[\"leerprobe\"] == \"minutes\", \"the kit probe is the minutes class\"\n    uebrig = {gid: cost for gid, cost in kosten.items() if gid not in (\"pytest\", \"leerprobe\")}\n    assert set(uebrig.values()) == {\"seconds\"}, uebrig\n    pytest_gate = next(g for g in doc[\"gates\"] if g[\"id\"] == \"pytest\")\n    assert \"runs it first\" not in pytest_gate[\"reason\"], \"the obsolete pytest-order claim must go with schema 3\"\n\n    v2 = copy.deepcopy(doc)\n    v2[\"schema_version\"] = 2\n    for g in v2[\"gates\"]:\n        g.pop(\"cost\", None)\n    assert ci_gates.validate_schema(v2), \"with schema 3 active, a version-2 list must be rejected, not accepted\"\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/verify-cheap-first/spec.md::Non-goals",
          "end_line": 146,
          "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- Speeding up successful gates, reducing test coverage, selecting gates\n  from changed files, caching results or promising a total runtime target.\n- Changing admission locks, worker sizing, duration storage schema,\n  targeted repair scheduling, hosted CI coverage or enforcement levels.\n- Automatic cost estimation, additional cost classes or sorting by live\n  timings. Future reclassification remains an explicit gate-list edit.\n- Migrating sibling repositories or reading or modifying a user-level stop\n  hook. Such a hook was not read in this worktree; compatibility beyond the\n  repository's output consumers is outside this change.\n- Design phase 2b and an ADR draft: this change retains class `bounded`,\n  for which the design phase does not run; the held gate-list edit still\n  makes the implementation a decision pull request.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/verify-cheap-first/spec.md",
          "reference": "Non-goals",
          "start_line": 132,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md",
          "reference": "The target picture",
          "start_line": 149,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
