          "excerpt": "duration_admission_context() {\n    if [ \"$1\" != \"${HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD:-}\" ]; then\n        unset HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_ID HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_WAIT 2>/dev/null || :\n    fi\n}\n\nif \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock --held >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    # A valid marker means this run nests in an admission an ancestor holds.\n    # One shape is the exception: when our parent IS the supervisor that holds\n    # the admission (the pid the holder published), this runner is the very\n    # command that admission admitted, and its fresh context — measured id and\n    # wait — is ours to record. Every genuinely nested run drops that context\n    # here, so its helpers resolve the shared wait from the validated\n    # ownership record and mark it reused instead of passing the ancestor's\n    # admission off as their own (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    duration_admission_context \"$PPID\"\nelse\n    exec \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock -- bash \"$PWD/scripts/verify_all.sh\" ${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]+\"${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]}\"}\nfi\n\n# ── Measured durations (bead coding-harness-1um6) ──────────────────────────\n#\n# One run identity per admitted runner, created here — after admission, before\n# the report and gate selection, so execution seconds cover both. The helper\n# scripts/verify_duration.py holds no gate command and reads no gate list: it\n# takes monotonic readings around the existing gate command, appends one JSON\n# line per event to the shared state root and refuses substituted\n# destinations. The admission supervisor's re-exec above\n# reaches this block once — the nested run inherits its ancestor's admission\n# and marks it reused instead of measuring a second wait.\nDUR_BROKEN=0\n# Runs in the parent shell (a $() subshell could not keep the flag), and\n# stores the helper's stdout in the named variable; the helper's own\n# diagnostics already went to stderr, visibly.\ndur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf lae",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_green_run_executes_every_selected_gate_once(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 5: a green run executes every selected gate exactly once — minutes gates included.\"\"\"\n    base = tmp_path / \"green\"\n    gates = [\n        _gate(base, \"slow-suite\", \"minutes\"),\n        _gate(base, \"fast-lint\", \"seconds\"),\n        _gate(base, \"fast-type\", \"seconds\"),\n        _gate(base, \"slow-probe\", \"minutes\"),\n    ]\n    tree = _tree_files(base / \"tree\")\n    _write_gate_file(tree, gates)\n    done = _run_runner(tree)\n    assert done.returncode == 0, f\"exit {done.returncode}\\n{done.stdout}\\n{done.stderr}\"\n    assert \"VERIFY GREEN\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    assert \"not run\" not in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    order = (base / \"order.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert order == \"fast-lint\\nfast-type\\nslow-suite\\nslow-probe\\n\", order\n    for gid in (\"slow-suite\", \"fast-lint\", \"fast-type\", \"slow-probe\"):\n        assert (base / f\"{gid}.ran\").exists(), gid\n        assert f\"── [{gid}] gruen\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n        assert re.search(rf\"── \\[{gid}\\] [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+s\", done.stdout), done.stdout\n    events = _tree_history(tree)\n    executed = [e[\"gate\"] for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert executed == [\"fast-lint\", \"fast-type\", \"slow-suite\", \"slow-probe\"], events\n    assert [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"run_end\"][0][\"verdict\"] == \"green\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_records_bind_results_to_revision_and_configuration(\n    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A record names its commit, dirty state, gate configuration, job and the command's raw exit.\n\n    Fault this pins: runs of different jobs or dirty trees becoming\n    indistinguishable, or a failed command losing its exit status in history.\n    \"\"\"\n    state = tmp_path / \"state\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    (repo / \"decisions\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    gate_file = repo / \"decisions\" / \"gates.yaml\"\n    gate_file.write_text(\"gates: []\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)\n\n    commits = iter([\"a\" * 40, \"b\" * 40])\n    porcelains = iter([\"\", \" M scripts/x.py\"])\n\n    def fake_git(arguments: list[str]) -> str | None:\n        if arguments == [\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]:\n            return next(commits, None)\n        if arguments == [\"status\", \"--porcelain\"]:\n            return next(porcelains, None)\n        return None\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(verify_duration, \"_git\", fake_git)\n\n    code, first, _ = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"verify\", \"--placement\", \"local\")\n    assert code == 0\n    started = _history(state)[-1]\n    assert started[\"run_id\"] == first.strip()\n    assert started[\"commit\"] == \"a\" * 40 and started[\"dirty\"] is False\n    assert started[\"config_sha256\"] == hashlib.sha256(gate_file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n    assert started[\"repository\"] == str(repo)\n    assert started[\"utc\"].endswith(\"+00:00\"), started[\"utc\"]\n\n    code, second, _ = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"docs\", \"--placement\", \"ci\")\n    assert code == 0\n    started = _history(state)[-1]\n    assert started[\"commit\"] == \"b\" * 40 and started[\"dirty\"] is True, (\n        \"a dirty tree must be distinguishable from a clean one\"\n    )\n\n    # A failed gate keeps its raw exit status — an advisory failure is not a pass.\n    code, _, _ = _run(\n        capsys,\n        \"gate\",\n        \"--run\",\n        first.strip(),\n        \"--gate\",\n        \"probe\",\n        \"--start\",\n        \"0.0\",\n        \"--end\",\n        \"2.0\",\n        \"--status\",\n        \"3\",\n        \"--enforcement\",\n        \"advisory\",\n    )\n    assert code == 0\n    gates = [event for event in _history(state) if event[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert len(gates) == 1\n    assert gates[0][\"exit\"] == 3 and gates[0][\"enforcement\"] == \"advisory\" and gates[0][\"seconds\"] == 2.0\n\n    # The two runs stay distinguishable in the listing.\n    code, out, _ = _run(capsys, \"report\")\n    assert code == 0\n    lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith(\"run \")]\n    assert len(lines) == 2\n    assert any(\"job verify\" in line for line in lines) and any(\"job docs\" in line for line in lines)\n    assert any(\"placement ci\" in line for line in lines)\n",

          "excerpt": "def cmd_start(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create one run identity and append its start record with the machine context.\"\"\"\n    memory = verify_lock.read_available_memory()\n    porcelain = _git([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n    event = {\n        \"v\": EVENT_VERSION,\n        \"event\": RUN_START,\n        \"run_id\": uuid.uuid4().hex,\n        \"utc\": _utc_now(),\n        \"repository\": str(Path.cwd()),\n        \"commit\": _git([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]),\n        # None means git could not answer; only an answer decides yes or no.\n        \"dirty\": None if porcelain is None else bool(porcelain),\n        \"config_sha256\": _gate_file_digest(),\n        \"job\": args.job,\n        \"placement\": args.placement,\n        \"memory_pct\": memory,\n        \"workers\": _worker_setting(),\n        **_context_fields(),\n    }\n    append_event(event)\n    print(event[\"run_id\"])\n    return 0\n",

          "excerpt": "def verify_evidence(done: subprocess.CompletedProcess, key: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The bounded evidence of a red post-run check (`make verify`, or the draft's document check).\n\n    It renders the framed gates that blocked, else the run's tail.\n\n    Read the active denylist at diagnostic emission time and raise Refused fail-closed if\n    protection refuses, on every route including keyless routes (key=None). The complete\n    concatenated streams are checked before reduction; their mapped boundary retains framing.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Protected whole, before any reduction: a cut must not split a multiline match and leave a part of it.\n    raw_stdout = done.stdout or \"\"\n    output, boundary = _protect_diagnostics(raw_stdout + (done.stderr or \"\"), key, len(raw_stdout))\n    stdout, stderr = output[:boundary], output[boundary:]\n    # verify_all.sh frames gates on standard output; a gate's standard error arrives unframed after them.\n    red = red_sections(stdout)\n    if red is None:\n        return scrub(\"\\n\".join(output.splitlines()[-TAIL_LINES:]), key)\n    evidence = \"The gates that blocked, each with its last lines:\\n\" + red\n    errors = stderr.splitlines()\n    if errors:\n        # Unframed: the last lines of the whole run's standard error, not of the blocking gate alone.\n        cut = len(errors) - STDERR_LINES\n        kept = ([f\"[… {cut} earlier lines left out …]\"] if cut > 0 else []) + errors[-STDERR_LINES:]\n        evidence += \"\\n\\nStandard error of the whole run, last lines:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(kept)\n    return scrub(evidence, key)\n",

          "end_line": 520,
          "excerpt": "class WorktreeSnapshot(Snapshot):\n    \"\"\"The files of the working tree: tracked and non-ignored untracked paths, read from disk.\n\n    The adapter the stage-2 runner uses to see links an uncommitted repair creates; the command\n    line stays on committed objects. A path deleted on disk is absent; a link, or a file whose\n    real path leaves the worktree, is never read. A source that cannot be read raises\n    `CannotMeasure`, so a caller never mistakes an unreadable inventory for zero links.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, repo: str, *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None, timeout: int = 120) -> None:\n        self.env = env\n        self.timeout = timeout\n        self.repo = repo\n        self.rev = \"worktree\"\n        self._blobs: dict[str, str] = {}  # path -> path, regular files only\n        self._read: dict[str, Source] | None = None\n        root = Path(repo).resolve()\n        listing = self._git([\"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\"])\n        names = {inventory_path(raw) for raw in listing.split(b\"\\0\") if raw}\n        paths = []\n        for path in sorted(names):\n            full = root / path\n            try:\n                info = full.lstat()\n            except FileNotFoundError:\n                continue  # deleted in the working tree\n            except OSError as err:\n                raise CannotMeasure(f\"cannot inspect {path}: {err.strerror or err}\") from err\n            paths.append(path)\n            if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):\n                if not full.resolve().is_relative_to(root):\n                    raise CannotMeasure(f\"{path} resolves outside the worktree\")\n                self._blobs[path] = path\n        self._index(paths)\n\n    def _load(self) -> dict[str, Source]:\n        out: dict[str, Source] = {}\n        root = Path(self.repo)\n        for path in self.sources:\n            try:\n                body = (root / path).read_bytes()\n            except OSError as err:\n                raise CannotMeasure(f\"cannot read {path}: {err.strerror or err}\") from err\n            out[path] = read_code(path, body.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\"))\n        return out\n",

      "statement": "Result storage is machine-wide and per user, outside the repository: the shared state root is `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness`, described as not identified by repository or worktree, and the history appends one JSON line per event under an exclusive flock keyed only by a fresh `run_id`. Concurrent admitted runs from different worktrees or repositories therefore write into the same file, and nothing in a start record refuses a dirty tree, so a lookup built from commit and gate configuration alone could pick up an end record written by another checkout or by a run over an uncommitted tree."

          "excerpt": "dur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32). Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"\necho \"── gates: job=$JOB ──────────────────────────────────────────────\"\n\n# The commands come out of the one list — id, enforcement, command, per tab.\n# The runner respects the vocabulary: only `block` turns the run red,\n# `report`/`advisory` speak up without blocking.\nfehler=0\nstop_gate=\"\"\nverbleibend=\"\"\nwhile IFS=\"$(printf '\\t')\" read -r gid enf cmd; do\n    [ -z \"$cmd\" ] && continue\n    # Cheap-first stop (bead coding-harness-bxxt.1): after the first blocking\n    # failure no further selected gate runs. The remaining ids are collected\n    # from the already obtained TSV and named in one summary below the loop;\n    # `--ci` never sets stop_gate and keeps running every selected gate.\n    if [ \"$CI_MODE\" -ne 1 ] && [ -n \"$stop_gate\" ]; then\n        verbleibend=\"${verbleibend}${gid}\n\"\n        continue\n    fi\n    # Werkzeuge aus dem Pin aufloesen (gates.md G-12): `python3` in der Liste\n    # heisst \"der gepinnte Interpreter\", nicht \"was der PATH gerade hergibt\".\n    # Die CI macht dasselbe ueber setup-python mit derselben Version.\n    # Quoted for `sh -c`: an absolute path may hold a space; a quote inside it is escaped.\n    python_word=\"'$(printf %s \"$PYTHON\" | sed \"s/'/'\\\\\\\\''/g\")'\"\n    lauf_cmd=${cmd/python3/\"$python_word\"}\n    echo \"\"\n    # Keep machine-local interpreter paths out of logs and repair evidence.\n    echo \"── [$gid] $ $cmd\"\n    # Monotonic readings immediately around the unchanged gate command; the\n    # raw status is captured before any timing operation, so it is the gate\n    # command's own and not a helper's (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    g_secs=\"\"\n    dur_call g_t0 clock\n    sh -c \"$lauf_cmd\"\n    gate_status=$?\n    dur_call g_t1 clock\n    if [ -n \"$RUN_ID\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t0\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t1\" ]; then\n        dur_call g_secs gate --run \"$RUN_ID\" --gate \"$gid\" --start \"$g_t0\" --end \"$g_t1\" --status \"$gate_status\" --enforcement \"$enf\"\n    fi\n    if [ \"$gate_status\" -eq 0 ]; then\n        echo \"── [$gid] gruen\"\n    elif [ \"$enf\" = \"block\" ]; then\n        fehler=1\n        # `--ci` stays exhaust",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"\necho \"── gates: job=$JOB ──────────────────────────────────────────────\"\n\n# The commands come out of the one list — id, enforcement, command, per tab.\n# The runner respects the vocabulary: only `block` turns the run red,\n# `report`/`advisory` speak up without blocking.\nfehler=0\nstop_gate=\"\"\nverbleibend=\"\"\nwhile IFS=\"$(printf '\\t')\" read -r gid enf cmd; do\n    [ -z \"$cmd\" ] && continue\n    # Cheap-first stop (bead coding-harness-bxxt.1): after the first blocking\n    # failure no further selected gate runs.           "excerpt": "def gates() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Alle Gates der einen Liste, in ihrer Reihenfolge.\"\"\"\n    fehler = validate_schema()\n    if fehler:\n        raise ValueError(\"Gate-Datei verletzt das Schema: \" + \"; \".join(fehler))\n    doc = yaml.safe_load(GATE_FILE.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for g in doc[\"gates\"]:\n        aktion = g.get(\"action\")\n        kommando = g.get(\"command\")\n        ersatz = _lokales_kommando(aktion, g.get(\"with\")) if aktion else None\n        out.append(\n            {\n                \"id\": g[\"id\"],\n                \"name\": g[\"title\"],\n                \"job\": g[\"job\"],\n                \"command\": kommando if kommando else ersatz,\n                \"action\": aktion,\n                \"with\": g.get(\"with\") or {},\n                \"enforcement\": g[\"enforcement\"],\n                \"floor\": g[\"floor\"],\n                \"placement\": g[\"placement\"],\n                \"cost\": g[\"cost\"],\n                \"needs_tracker\": bool(g.get(\"needs_tracker\")),\n                \"needs_history\": bool(g.get(\"needs_history\")),\n                \"subsets\": list(g.get(\"subsets\") or []),\n                \"reason\": g.get(\"reason\", \"\"),\n                \"local_runnable\": kommando is not None or ersatz is not None,\n                \"via_local_equivalent\": ersatz is not None,\n            }\n        )\n    return out\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5)",

          "excerpt": "def test_history_rejects_substituted_destinations(\n    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A symlink or FIFO standing where the history belongs refuses; nothing is written through it.\n\n    Fault this pins: an append following a substituted file to its target, a\n    FIFO in the file's place hanging the runner, or an aliased state root\n    being written into at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    root = tmp_path / \"state\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    root.mkdir(parents=True)\n\n    # A symlink in the file's place: the victim keeps its bytes, the op refuses.\n    victim = tmp_path / \"victim.jsonl\"\n    victim.write_text(\"do not write through me\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (root / verify_duration.HISTORY_NAME).symlink_to(victim)\n    code, _, err = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"verify\", \"--placement\", \"local\")\n    assert code == 2 and \"substituted\" in err, err\n    assert victim.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"do not write through me\\n\"\n\n    # A FIFO in the file's place: refused without waiting on a writer that never comes.\n    (root / verify_duration.HISTORY_NAME).unlink()\n    os.mkfifo(root / verify_duration.HISTORY_NAME)\n    code, _, err = _run(\n        capsys,\n        \"gate\",\n        \"--run\",\n        \"some-run\",\n        \"--gate\",\n        \"probe\",\n        \"--start\",\n        \"0.0\",\n        \"--end\",\n        \"1.0\",\n        \"--status\",\n        \"0\",\n        \"--enforcement\",\n        \"block\",\n    )\n    assert code == 2 and \"substituted\" in err, err\n\n    # The whole state root as a symlink: the aliased target is never touched.\n    target = tmp_path / \"elsewhere\"\n    target.mkdir()\n    (target / \"sentinel.txt\").write_text(\"do not touch\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    aliased = tmp_path / \"aliased-state\"\n    aliased.mkdir()\n    (aliased / \"coding-harness\").symlink_to(target)\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\", str(aliased))\n    code, _, err = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"verify\", \"--placement\", \"local\")\n    assert code == 2 and \"not a usable directory\" in err, err\n    assert (target / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"do not touch\"\n    assert not (target / verify_duration.HISTORY_NAME).exists(), \"the aliased state root was written through\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_unusable_or_aliased_state_refuses_before_work(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Substituted or unusable state refuses with a diagnostic before work, never runs unlocked.\n\n    Fault this pins: falling through unlocked after a state, lock or queue\n    error, or following a substituted file to overwrite another file.\n    \"\"\"\n    monkeypatch.delenv(verify_lock.LOCK_ENV, raising=False)\n\n    def refuses(state: Path) -> None:\n        monkeypatch.setenv(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\", str(state))\n        with pytest.raises(verify_lock.VerifyLockRefused), verify_lock.hold_admission([\"refused\", \"work\"]):\n            raise AssertionError(\"protected work ran on refused admission\")\n\n    # the whole state root as a symlink: the target's file is never written through\n    target = tmp_path / \"elsewhere\"\n    target.mkdir()\n    (target / \"sentinel.txt\").write_text(\"do not touch\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    aliased = tmp_path / \"state-aliased\"\n    aliased.mkdir()\n    (aliased / \"coding-harness\").symlink_to(target)\n    refuses(aliased)\n    assert (target / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"do not touch\"\n    assert not (target / verify_lock.LOCK_NAME).exists(), \"the aliased state root was written through\"\n\n    # a lock file substituted by a symlink: refusal, and the victim keeps its bytes\n    plain = tmp_path / \"state-lock\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    plain.mkdir(parents=True)\n    victim = tmp_path / \"victim.txt\"\n    victim.write_text(\"victim\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (plain / verify_lock.LOCK_NAME).symlink_to(victim)\n    refuses(tmp_path / \"state-lock\")\n    assert victim.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"victim\", \"the substituted lock's target was modified\"\n\n    # a queue directory substituted by a symlink refuses as well\n    queue_alias = tmp_path",

          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-verify-machine-lock/spec.md::Acceptance criteria",
          "end_line": 133,
          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When independent protected entries use the same shared state, at most one\n   admission's protected work executes at a time across repositories and worktrees.\n   *Refuted by:* overlapping gate/pytest intervals from independent admissions.\n\n2. When several live entries wait, they are admitted in registration order\n   without runner priority.\n   *Refuted by:* a later registered waiter overtaking an earlier live waiter.\n\n3. While an entry waits for another holder, it logs the wait immediately and\n   at least every five minutes, identifying the holder's process id, command\n   and start time whenever a holder exists.\n   *Refuted by:* a silent wait, a missing five-minute update, or missing holder\n   identity despite an active holder with published metadata.\n\n4. When a runner check finally starts, its configured execution time limit\n   is available in full regardless of time spent in admission.\n   *Refuted by:* queue or memory waiting causing a short passing check to time\n   out, or removal of the existing limit on a hung executing check.\n\n5. When nested work inherits a valid held marker, it uses its ancestor's\n   admission without another queue or memory wait.\n   *Refuted by:* a nested copied runner deadlocking or rechecking memory; an\n   absent, malformed, stale or unrelated marker bypassing admission.\n\n6. When a protected invocation finishes, fails or is interrupted, remaining\n   live waiters can proceed without manual stale-lock or dead-waiter cleanup.\n   *Refuted by:* a dead holder/waiter blocking progress, or releasing ownership\n   while its protected child workload still runs.\n\n7. When a memory reading is available, admission uses macOS\n   `memory_pressure`'s system-wide free percentage or Linux\n   `MemAvailable / MemTotal * 100`, according to the host platform.\n   *Refuted by:* substituting another macOS percentage, Linux `MemFree`, or\n   accepting malformed/non-finite values as a usable reading.\n\n8. While usable available-memory readings are below the configured floor,\n   admission retains the lock and waits, logging and rechecking every 30 seconds.\n   *Refuted by:* protected work starting on a below-floor reading or another\n   admission entering while the first waits for memory.\n\n9. If usable memory readings remain below the floor for 60 minutes from the\n   first low reading, admission refuses without starting protected work and\n   names the floor and last reading.\n   *Refuted by:* a workload starting, an unbounded low-memory wait, or refusal\n   without the two percentages; a qualifying reading before the deadline must\n   instead allow work to start.\n\n10. If memory cannot be measured, admission logs that fact and proceeds.\n    *Refuted by:* an unavailable, failed, hung, unsupported or malformed probe\n    hanging/refusing the run or being silently treated as a valid percentage.\n\n11. When no override is provided, the floor is 25 percent, with equality\n    sufficient for admission.\n    *Refuted by:* a usable reading below 25 starting work, or exactly 25 waiting.\n\n12. When `HARNESS_VERIFY_MEMORY_FLOOR` supplies a finite percentage in\n    `[0, 100]`, admission uses that value; an invalid override refuses explicitly.\n    *Refuted by:* ignoring a valid override or silently accepting an invalid one.\n\n13. When protected work completes, the wrapper preserves its existing success\n    or failure verdict and gate selection, including hosted CI.\n    *Refuted by:* turning a failed check green, changing placement/enforcement,\n    adding a second command list, or disabling admission merely because CI is set.\n\n14. If shared locking or queue state cannot be used safely, the entry refuses\n    with a diagnostic before protected work starts.\n    *Refuted by:* falling through unlocked after a state-directory, lock or\n    queue error, or following a substituted state file to overwrite another file.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "duration_admission_context() {\n    if [ \"$1\" != \"${HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD:-}\" ]; then\n        unset HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_ID HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_WAIT 2>/dev/null || :\n    fi\n}\n\nif \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock --held >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    # A valid marker means this run nests in an admission an ancestor holds.\n    # One shape is the exception: when our parent IS the supervisor that holds\n    # the admission (the pid the holder published), this runner is the very\n    # command that admission admitted, and its fresh context — measured id and\n    # wait — is ours to record. Every genuinely nested run drops that context\n    # here, so its helpers resolve the shared wait from the validated\n    # ownership record and mark it reused instead of passing the ancestor's\n    # admission off as their own (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    duration_admission_context \"$PPID\"\nelse\n    exec \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock -- bash \"$PWD/scripts/verify_all.sh\" ${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]+\"${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]}\"}\nfi\n\n# ── Measured durations (bead coding-harness-1um6) ──────────────────────────\n#\n# One run identity per admitted runner, created here — after admission, before\n# the report and gate selection, so execution seconds cover both. The helper\n# scripts/verify_duration.py holds no gate command and reads no gate list: it\n# takes monotonic readings around the existing gate command, appends one JSON\n# line per event to the shared state root and refuses substituted\n# destinations. A storage failure warns here and leaves the gates, their\n# enforcement and the verdict untouched; the run then records no history and\n# cannot supply a persisted baseline. The admission supervisor's re-exec above\n# reaches this block once — the nested run inherits its ancestor's admission\n# and marks it reused instead of measuring a second wait.\nDUR_BROKEN=0\n# Runs in the parent shell (a $() subshell could not keep the flag), and\n# stores the helper's stdout in the named variable; the helper's own\n# diagnostics already went to stderr, visibly.\ndur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32). Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"",

          "excerpt": "def test_unusable_or_aliased_state_refuses_before_work(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Substituted or unusable state refuses with a diagnostic before work, never runs unlocked.\n\n    Fault this pins: falling through unlocked after a state, lock or queue\n    error, or following a substituted file to overwrite another file.\n    \"\"\"\n    monkeypatch.delenv(verify_lock.LOCK_ENV, raising=False)\n\n    def refuses(state: Path) -> None:\n        monkeypatch.setenv(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\", str(state))\n        with pytest.raises(verify_lock.VerifyLockRefused), verify_lock.hold_admission([\"refused\", \"work\"]):\n            raise AssertionError(\"protected work ran on refused admission\")\n\n    # the whole state root as a symlink: the target's file is never written through\n    target = tmp_path / \"elsewhere\"\n    target.mkdir()\n    (target / \"sentinel.txt\").write_text(\"do not touch\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    aliased = tmp_path / \"state-aliased\"\n    aliased.mkdir()\n    (aliased / \"coding-harness\").symlink_to(target)\n    refuses(aliased)\n    assert (target / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"do not touch\"\n    assert not (target / verify_lock.LOCK_NAME).exists(), \"the aliased state root was written through\"\n\n    # a lock file substituted by a symlink: refusal, and the victim keeps its bytes\n    plain = tmp_path / \"state-lock\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    plain.mkdir(parents=True)\n    victim = tmp_path / \"victim.txt\"\n    victim.write_text(\"victim\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (plain / verify_lock.LOCK_NAME).symlink_to(victim)\n    refuses(tmp_path / \"state-lock\")\n    assert victim.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"victim\", \"the substituted lock's target was modified\"\n\n    # a queue directory substituted by a symlink refuses as well\n    queue_alias = tmp_path / \"state-queue\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    queue_alias.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (queue_alias / verify_lock.QUEUE_DIR).symlink_to(tmp_path)\n    refuses(tmp_path / \"state-queue\")\n\n    # an unwritable state root refuses rather than running without the lock\n    readonly = tmp_path / \"readonly\"\n    readonly.mkdir()\n    readonly.chmod(0o500)\n    try:\n        refuses(readonly)\n    finally:\n        readonly.chmod(0o700)\n\n    # the supervisor form refuses loudly instead of running the command unlocked\n    sabotaged = tmp_path / \"state-cli\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    sabotaged.mkdir(parents=True)\n    cli_victim = tmp_path / \"victim-cli.txt\"\n    cli_victim.write_text(\"victim\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (sabotaged / verify_lock.LOCK_NAME).symlink_to(cli_victim)\n    never = tmp_path / \"never.json\"\n    done = subprocess.run(\n        [\n            sys.executable,\n            \"-m\",\n            \"scripts.verify_lock\",\n            \"--\",\n            sys.executable,\n            \"-c\",\n            f\"import pathlib; pathlib.Path({str(never)!r}).write_text('ran', encoding='utf-8')\",\n        ],\n        cwd=REPO_ROOT,\n        env=_env(tmp_path / \"state-cli\"),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        timeout=60,\n    )\n    assert done.returncode == 2, f\"the supervisor did not refuse: {done.stderr}\"\n    assert \"refusing\" in done.stderr, f\"the refusal carries no diagnostic: {done.stderr}\"\n    assert not never.exists(), \"the refused command ran anyway\"\n",
